solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Musing, Mark stops downfall

indicators.note: the mark plugs a gap in the word for downfall, as a stopper fills a hole

parts.note: ruination is a total downfall or collapse
M stands for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone reflects while a mark interrupts a sudden collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminating is deep pondering, so the noun for it is a synonym of musing.

clue.text: Spread net that's deployed to save a life

definitions.text: that's deployed to save a life

parts.note: to air news or views is to spread them about
to net something is to catch it, which is also to bag it

explanation.surface: A safety net is spread out by rescuers to catch someone falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' reads as a noun with 'Spread' as its verb; both are really verbs giving the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's inflating cushion fires out in a crash to protect the occupants, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Pilot stripped for a girl

indicators.note: stripped means the word loses its outer layers, its first and last letters

parts.note: an airman is a pilot

explanation.surface: A pilot is stripped of rank for the sake of some girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' takes the A and N off each end of AIRMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in the film Irma la Douce.

clue.text: Ornamental feature of drink that's long and cool

parts.note: to neck a drink is to swig it down quickly
L is the abbreviation for long, as on clothing sizes
ace is slang for excellent or cool

explanation.surface: A tall, chilled drink served with a decorative touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long and cool' sounds like a description of the drink, but it gives L and ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of beads or chain worn round the throat is jewellery, an ornament.

clue.text: Reportedly try religious adherent

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the word, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: to seek is to try or attempt

explanation.surface: A news story says someone is putting a believer on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the faith founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab.

clue.text: He could transport van of Hugh Laurie after a crash

indicators.note: the van is the front, so it is the first letter of the actor's first name
a crash wrecks the surname's letters, which then take a new order

explanation.surface: The actor Hugh Laurie's van has been in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' looks like a vehicle, fitting the transport theme, but means the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A road haulage operator or lorry driver moves goods for a living.

clue.text: Examined axis of wheel with stiff bearing

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the word for stiff holds the other piece

parts.note: stiff means hard, as in hard to bend

indicators.note: an axis runs through the centre, so this takes the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: An engineer inspects a wheel's axle with a stiff bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like part of a wheel; here it means carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who has heard a case has tried or examined it in court.

clue.text: Michael sent back old computer

indicators.note: sent back means the surname is written in the reverse direction

parts.note: Michael Caine is the British film actor

explanation.surface: Someone called Michael returns an outdated computer.
explanation.definitionFit: An early American electronic computer of the 1940s, so a historic machine.

clue.text: Char caught by bank about to be served up

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an aircraft banks when it leans or tilts

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word goes upwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A burnt piece of fish is caught at the riverbank and will soon be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like the fish or burning; it is the British word for a charwoman, a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A char is a charwoman, a woman paid to do housework.

clue.text: Regularly penalizing extremist

indicators.note: regularly here takes letter pairs at even intervals, dropping the pairs between

explanation.surface: A zealot who keeps imposing penalties on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' keeps pairs of letters in turn: pe-NA-li-ZI-ng.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Hitler's party, and loosely any far-right fanatic.

clue.text: Ban a female with a record, a disreputable one

parts.note: to black something is to boycott or ban it, as unions black goods
she is a female person
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A woman with a criminal record is barred as disreputable.
explanation.definitionFit: The family member who brings disgrace is an idiomatic disreputable person.

clue.text: Fish eating seaweed that's chemically perfect?

indicators.note: eating means the fish take the seaweed inside them

parts.note: ides are freshwater fish, the plural of ide
an alga is a seaweed

explanation.surface: Fish feeding on seaweed are an ideal sight to a chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoretical gas whose molecules obey the gas laws exactly is the perfect model in chemistry.

clue.text: Myths from the north or south?

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same whether read up from the bottom or down from the top

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Legends that come from northern or southern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: The north suggests Norse legends, but the word reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Long heroic tales, as in Icelandic literature, are legends or myths.

clue.text: Brief entry record about company's port

indicators.note: about means round, the cut record surrounding the firm
brief means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: an annal is the record of a single year's entry in a chronicle
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A short entry in the record of a company's harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaport on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Panic as drunken European interrupts odd bits of Swan Lake

indicators.note: drunken means the letters reel about into a new order
interrupts means one letter breaks into the pair of letters
odd bits are the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tipsy European causes panic at a performance of the ballet Swan Lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan Lake' reads as the ballet, but 'Lake' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's largest inland body of water is technically a lake despite its name.

clue.text: Alcohol found in fruit salad from the east

indicators.note: from the east says the hidden letters are read backwards
found in says the letters are sitting inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some alcohol has been tipped into the fruit salad.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Alcohol found' as the definition, but 'found in' marks where the letters sit, leaving 'Alcohol' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Opening present, endlessly slippery

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone opens a gift that keeps slipping out of their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but means here.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word as an adjective meaning slithery or slippery.

clue.text: Missing a note, make a mess of horn

indicators.note: missing means the note is lost from the word

parts.note: to bungle is to make a mess of a task
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A player fluffs a note and makes a mess of the horn part.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument used for military calls is a kind of horn.

clue.text: Court attendant's large outfit is returned after dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: is returned means the two pieces are written backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing
a rig is an outfit of clothing

explanation.surface: A courtier's oversized outfit is sent back after the royal dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a palace; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl who fetches stray balls during a tennis match attends on the court.

clue.text: Son runs into fat pig with sides splitting dress

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the pair of middles
sides splitting means each word loses its outer letters, leaving its centre

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A boy runs into a fat pig and splits his sides laughing, wearing a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with sides splitting' suggests laughter; it strips the ends off 'fat' and 'pig', leaving A and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapped garment worn by women in South Asia is a dress.

clue.text: Blair possibly isolated by Left for including independent

indicators.note: including means the letter for independent sits inside

parts.note: lone means isolated, alone

explanation.surface: Tony Blair is cut off by the Left for including independents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' suggests Tony Blair, the Labour prime minister; it is Lionel Blair, a British television entertainer and dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the entertainer Blair, so a name one Blair possibly has.

clue.text: Starts to survey peeper, one endlessly enjoying short slip

indicators.note: starts are first letters, taken from the two words that follow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: liking means enjoying

explanation.surface: A voyeur begins to survey the scene, enjoying a brief glimpse of a petticoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillikin is a small thin strip of wood or bone, as used in the game of jackstraws.

clue.text: Concerned with young one's nightmares

parts.note: in means involved or concerned with, as in being in a scheme
a cub is a young animal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bad dreams that come from worry about a young child.
explanation.definitionFit: Demons thought to lie on sleepers; the old word incubus also meant a nightmare.

clue.text: Religious men primarily instil morals, averting mortal sin

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Preachers mainly teach morals so that people avoid mortal sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslim prayer leaders are religious men.

clue.text: Appealing in print

parts.note: print suggests books, but a photographic print is meant: someone who looks good in photographs

explanation.surface: Writing that is attractive once it is published.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who comes out well in photographs is attractive in a photo print.

clue.text: Fairly big documents finally put away for wrapping

indicators.note: wrapping means the two final letters go round the papers
finally takes the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: ID is identification documents

explanation.surface: Large documents are finally put away in wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a considerable amount, so the word means fairly large.

clue.text: Native American mostly cut out foreign food

indicators.note: mostly cut out means most of the letters in the middle of the phrase are removed

explanation.surface: A Native American mostly avoids eating foreign food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly cut out' removes TIVE AMERIC, keeping NA from 'Native' and AN from 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leavened flatbread from Indian cuisine, so food from abroad.

clue.text: Chap having a turn, stopped by a seizure in court

indicators.note: stopped by means the reversed word is plugged by the letter
having a turn means the word is turned round backwards

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man has a funny turn, stopped by a seizure in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizure' suggests a fit; it is the legal sense of seizing goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An old legal term for distraint, the taking of goods by legal order.

clue.text: Remove limits in escalator clause

parts.note: to rid is to remove or clear away

indicators.note: limits are the outer edges, the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone wants the cost-escalation term taken out of a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escalator clause' looks like one phrase, but 'escalator' supplies letters and 'clause' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An added provision attached to a bill or contract is an extra clause.

clue.text: Those taking it easy lost marbles

indicators.note: lost means the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: People who are relaxing have lost their marbles.
explanation.definitionFit: People strolling at a leisurely pace are taking it easy.
